Since both rewards are computed only during training, CoFiBreak also retains inference efficiency. Trained with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as the victim, CoFiBreak discovers 1.6-2.0x as many distinct successful fine-grained strategies as the strongest baseline across frontier victims on HarmBench. It reaches 98.8% ASR@10 (attack success rate with 10 generations per intent) on AdvBench with the highest diversity score among all compared methods, which is 2.1x that of the strongest-attacking baseline. The resulting attacks transfer to unseen frontier LLMs, reaching 71.0% ASR@10 on AdvBench with the unseen victim Claude-Opus-4.6. The code will be released.
items.author: Jialin Song, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang, Mingqian Feng, Chengquan Guo, Qiyao Ma, Carolyn Buractaon, Anson Ho, Wuyang Chen, Christopher White

items.title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.40893v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. We present Qistas (Arabic qistas, "the just balance"), a protocol for evaluating how LLMs treat the social, confessional, and regional constituencies of a society, portable across countries and instantiated first for Iraq. In its pilot form it measures only what needs no verdict on contested truth: procedural symmetry across matched counterfactual pairs, differential refusal, stereotype reliance under ambiguity, and terminological framing of documented events. Every measurement is paired by construction and analysed with paired machinery (sign-flip permutation tests, exact McNemar tests, template-clustered bootstrap intervals, Holm-corrected families), with a power analysis that states, before any data exist, the smallest effect each axis can detect after the design effect of template clustering. We release the authoring apparatus (a pruned 3x5 taxonomy with four cells closed by design, per-type checklists, a cumulative rulings log, a structural audit, and a human review notebook) and report its first field test: a semantic review of a 58-item seed bank in which 24 of 25 template groups failed at least one check. The defect patterns it exposed (evaluation criteria leaking into prompts, token-level swaps that break Arabic agreement, epistemically unbalanced pairs, single-theme refusal probes, unwritten dialect twins counted as coverage) are, we argue, general hazards of counterfactual fairness benchmarks. This is a protocol paper, not a results paper: no model has been evaluated, and the accompanying pre-registration commits the hypotheses, metrics, exclusion rules, and analysis plan that the pilot will follow.
items.author: Nawar S. Alseelawi, Mustafa S. Aljumaily

items.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.34599v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Despite advances in automated liver lesion segmentation, a gap remains between image-derived predictions and clinically interpretable radiology reports. Bridging this gap requires quantitative measurements that are both reproducible and traceable. We present an evidence-grounded agentic AI framework that connects liver and lesion segmentation with deterministic quantification and structured reporting. TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models delineate the liver, Couinaud segments, and lesions, while computational tools extract volumes, dimensions, counts, and anatomical locations. A large language model (LLM) organizes these measurements into a predefined reporting schema, with numerical consistency checks against source measurements. On 51 LiTS cases, the segmentation stage achieved a liver Dice score of 0.947, lesion sensitivity of 75.6%, and positive predictive value of 68.9%. Exploratory screening of 25,494 MERLIN reports identified 10,208 (40.0%) with liver-related abnormalities. By connecting quantitative imaging evidence with agentic report generation, this work takes a step toward human-centered medical AI that prioritizes traceability and clinical relevance.
items.author: Fatma Ahmed Mansour, Rahatara Ferdousi, Manar Fathy Elshenawy

items.title: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model
items.summary:
arXiv:2609.30215v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We prove nearly quadratic lower bounds for randomized algorithms for linear optimization and uniform sampling over convex bodies in the membership oracle model. For linear optimization, this matches the known nearly quadratic upper bound up to a polylog factor in the dimension. For uniform sampling, this improves on the previous linear lower bound. Our construction also implies the same lower bound for volume estimation.
items.author: Santosh S. Vempala

items.title: Minimax Alternating Regret for the Experts Problem and Online Convex Optimization
items.summary:
arXiv:2608.25182v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In this paper, we study alternating regret in online convex optimization (OCO), motivated by the success of alternating learning dynamics in two-player games. Although previous works have shown that $o(\sqrt{T})$ alternating regret is achievable under various assumptions on the loss functions and feasible domains, the minimax regret rate has remained open even for the expert problem. In this paper, we resolve this question by showing matching lower and upper bounds for both the expert problem and general OCO. Somewhat surprisingly, for the $d$-expert problem, we show that the minimax alternating regret is $\Theta(\log d)$ by providing both a lower bound and an algorithm achieving a matching upper bound. This significantly improves upon the $O(T^{1/3}\log^{2/3} d)$ established by [HLLZ25]. We further extend our results to general OCO over a $d$-dimensional compact convex set and prove that the worst-case minimax alternating regret is $\Theta\left(d\log \left(1+\frac{T}{d}\right)\right)$, also significantly improving upon the $O((d\log T)^{2/3}T^{1/3})$ upper bound and resolving the open problem posed by [CCK+23,HLLZ25]. As a direct implication, our alternating dynamics achieve $O(\frac{\log d}{T})$ convergence to Nash equilibrium in two-player zero-sum games, matching the state of the art, and give the first such convergence rate to coarse correlated equilibrium in two-player general-sum games. Technically, our upper bound for the expert problem is achieved by a corrected variant of Hedge. We extend the same corrected-potential argument to continuous action sets to obtain the optimal alternating-regret rate for OCO. For the lower bounds, the construction for the expert problem repeatedly eliminates half of the candidate experts, while the OCO lower bound instance construction replaces this discrete elimination by a more involved multiscale construction on the unit disk.
items.author: Mengxiao Zhang

items.title: You Only Pass Once: Answering and Abstaining Together in a Single Forward Pass of a Frozen Language Model
items.summary:
arXiv:2608.14465v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: A frozen language model under-uses the evidence in its hidden states and answers confidently when the context contains no answer. We fix both on the residual stream without changing any weight. For accuracy, a small trained network (the probe) adds an input-dependent vector to the residual at several middle layers; it raises Qwen2.5-1.5B on $\alpha$NLI from 51% to 73% accuracy. For abstention, a fixed vector (the direction), the mean hidden state of contexts that contain the answer minus that of contexts that do not, scores the hidden state; a low score abstains. On four QA datasets with human answerability labels (Qwen2.5-7B), moving the direction to a dataset it was not fit on costs under 3 points of decision accuracy (from 0.83 in domain) on average and still beats asking the model whether its context suffices; the same judgment trained as a classifier into the probe's activation edit or into LoRA weights loses 16 and 22 points and ends below asking. We set out to put both functions on a single forward pass, and found that the probe's edit changes the very hidden state the direction scores, degrading it. A small map -- trained without labels, only to reconstruct the unedited hidden state from the edited one -- removes 63% of that interference on 1.5B. Refit on the hidden-state pairs of LoFiT or LoReFT, the same recipe repairs those methods too: the steering module is replaceable. The resulting system, YOPO, answers and abstains in one forward pass. On $\alpha$NLI it raises three-way accuracy from 0.38 to about 0.75 on 1.5B, and stays within 0.02 of a two-pass reference on 1.5B, 3B and 7B, at half the cost. We also observe improvements on the four QA datasets, where answerability is human-labeled and answers are generated as free-form text. Near-parity with the two-pass reference holds across nine backbones spanning six model families without backbone-specific hyperparameter tuning.
items.author: Ziyang Luo, Zhongyao Chu, Xinjie He, Youting Wang, Xukui Qin, Runxiong Wu, Yan-Syuan Chen

items.title: How Much Reconstruction Does Quantum Machine Learning Need? Late Fusion of Uncoupled Quantum Subcircuits
items.summary:
arXiv:2608.05595v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Circuit cutting lets a large quantum neural network (QNN) run as independent subcircuits on small devices, but rebuilding its outputs by quasiprobability reconstruction carries a classical sampling overhead exponential in the number of cuts. This paper asks whether machine-learning tasks need this step. We replace it with late fusion: subcircuits are trained without cross-cut coupling, and a small classical head combines their local measurements at a cost constant in the cut count. To characterize the trade-off, we introduce a reconstruction dial $Q$, a physically executable budget that retains a fraction of the quasiprobability terms, and a cut-entanglement diagnostic that indicates, within a fixed scale, how much reconstruction a task needs (Spearman $\rho=0.59$ over $104$ runs). Across synthetic and standard datasets, uncoupled late fusion is equivalent to full reconstruction within a predefined margin of $0.02$ accuracy on most benchmarks and pooled over the controlled sweep, at exponentially lower cost; deficits of $0.02$-$0.04$ remain on the most cross-cut tasks. Fusion tops the dial's accuracy/cost frontier, is more robust to shot and device noise, and loses nothing as the coupled model's entangling depth grows. We state the exact condition under which fusion must lose accuracy, a decision-relevant cross-cut correlator, and realize it with entangled-state inputs; for classical inputs the register partition discards no information. We claim no advantage over classical machine learning.
items.author: Prabhjot Singh, Adel N. Toosi, Rajkumar Buyya

items.title: Fields of the Planet: Field Boundary Mapping Beyond 10m
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.04449v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Field-boundary accuracy depends on the model, sensor resolution, label discretization, and evaluation procedure. Measuring the contribution of sensor resolution therefore requires a controlled comparison across sensors. We present Fields of the Planet (FTP), a 3 m PlanetScope companion to Fields of The World (FTW) containing 133,168 co-registered patch-window targets across 24 countries. FTP preserves FTW's vector polygons, seasonal windows, and dataset splits, enabling direct comparison with 10 m Sentinel-2. We first quantify the resolution ceiling by rasterizing and vectorizing the same ground-truth parcels at each resolution to determine which fields the label grid can represent. We evaluate predicted parcels with polygon-level and boundary metrics. With identical PRUE+ training and post-processing across sensors, plus an upsampled Sentinel-2 control, we isolate gains from image content. PlanetScope raises panoptic quality (PQ) from 21.0 to 35.5, improves PQ on sub-$0.5$ ha fields from 5.8 to 15.7, and reduces matched-boundary error from 18.6 m to 7.4 m. Pixel-level metrics understate this improvement, so field-boundary benchmarks should account for sensor resolution.
items.author: Isaac Corley, Caleb Robinson, Hannah Kerner, Jennifer Marcus

items.title: Soft Mixture-of-Recursions: Going Deeper with Recursive Vision Transformers
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.00774v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Vision Transformers are typically scaled by increasing depth or width, at the cost of more unique parameters. We explore recursion as an alternative scaling axis that increases effective computational depth through parameter reuse. Yet simply increasing recursion depth does not reliably improve performance because representations from different recursion stages are not fully utilized. We propose Soft Mixture-of-Recursions (SoftMoR), which learns token-wise weights to combine representations across recursion steps, and instantiate it as the Soft Recursive Vision Transformer (SR-ViT). Experiments on ImageNet-1K, COCO, and ADE20K show that SR-ViT can benefit from deeper recursion while adding few parameters. On ImageNet-1K, increasing recursion depth from T=1 to T=3 improves top-1 accuracy from 79.83% to 82.45% with only 1.1M additional parameters. At matched effective depth, SR-ViT also outperforms independently parameterized counterparts with substantially fewer parameters. These results support recursive deepening as an effective, parameter-efficient scaling axis for Vision Transformers. The code is available at https://github.com/sangin-lee/sr-vit .
items.author: Sang In Lee, Jihun Park

items.title: No-Harm Physics-Informed Inverse Learning with Residual-Calibrated Uncertainty
items.summary:
arXiv:2606.07153v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Physics-informed learning is increasingly used for partial differential equation (PDE)-governed inverse problems, but its reliability remains difficult to certify. This paper develops a no-harm certification-and-selection framework for physics-informed inverse learning. A learned reconstruction is accepted only when its residual-calibrated radius is no worse than the baseline radius, namely when $$R_{\mathrm{learn}}\le R_{\mathrm{base}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{safe}};$$otherwise, the method returns the baseline. The certificate combines data, physics, boundary or initial-condition, and optimization residuals. Under a conditional stability estimate, these residuals yield an a posteriori reconstruction-error bound and a deterministic uncertainty radius. A high-probability certificate is also derived for physics residuals estimated from independent random collocation points. Numerical tests on Poisson source recovery, inverse heat reconstruction, limited-angle tomography, elliptic coefficient identification, and stochastic residual validation show that the selector accepts certified improvements, rejects shifted, hallucinated, or unfinished candidates, and becomes conservative in strongly ill-posed regimes. The framework is therefore a certification-and-selection layer, not another reconstruction architecture.
items.author: Ronald Katende

items.title: Accelerating Min-Max Optimization via Power-Law Stepsizes
items.summary:
arXiv:2606.01764v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We revisit the convergence guarantees of the Extragradient (EG) method for unconstrained biaffine min-max optimization. It is known that EG with a fixed stepsize achieves a $\Theta(T^{-1/2})$ last-iterate convergence rate, which is slower than the optimal $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate attainable by incorporating additional mechanisms such as anchoring. Motivated by recent advances showing that dynamic stepsizes alone can significantly accelerate gradient descent, we ask whether dynamic stepsizes can similarly accelerate the last-iterate convergence of EG.
  We present the first positive result in this direction. Specifically, we provide a deterministic dynamic stepsize schedule that accelerates the convergence rate of EG to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2/3+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$. We also show that this rate is nearly tight when the extrapolation and update steps of EG use the same stepsize. We then show that allowing different stepsizes for the extrapolation and update steps further improves the convergence rate to the near-optimal $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1+\varepsilon})$. Our analysis reduces stepsize scheduling to an optimization problem, whose solution leads to a stepsize schedule that follows (a discretization of) a power-law distribution. Our proposed stepsize schedules and analysis extend to other methods, such as Optimistic Gradient (OG), and suggest broader applicability to general min-max optimization problems.
items.author: Yue Wu, Weiqiang Zheng, Yang Cai, Haipeng Luo

items.title: Geometry of Relaxed Fair Regression: A Unified Framework for Aware and Unaware Settings
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.28233v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Fairness-accuracy trade-offs are a central concern in the deployment of fairness-aware machine learning methods. When sensitive attributes are unavailable at inference time-the so called unawareness setting, principled methods for obtaining accurate predictions under relaxed fairness constraints are largely missing. In this work, we address this gap by formulating regression under a demographic parity penalty as an optimal transport problem. Our framework, unifies both the aware and unaware settings and characterizes optimal prediction functions via optimal transport maps, under both squared Wasserstein-2 and Total Variation penalties. These results reveal that the choice of penalty reflects fundamentally different fairness philosophies: the Wasserstein penalty induces a smooth, population-wide compromise, while Total Variation enforces parity for a subset of individuals. Building on these theoretical characterizations, we propose FAUST, an algorithm that is simple to implement, computationally efficient, and consistently matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on real-world benchmarks.
items.author: Marie Generali Lince, Vincent Divol, R\'emi Flamary, Solenne Gaucher, Patrick Loiseau

items.title: Optimal Design for Multinomial Logit Model with Applications to Best Assortment Identification
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.25592v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study optimal experimental design for multinomial logit (MNL) bandits, where an agent repeatedly selects a subset of $K$ items from a ground set of size $N$ and observes single-choice feedback. Unlike linear or generalized linear bandits, MNL bandits have a combinatorial action space, which makes classical optimal design approaches and naive optimization over all subsets computationally intractable. We propose a computationally efficient optimal design framework for MNL models that achieves both statistical efficiency and scalability through two complementary approaches: (i) an exact or certified-approximate reformulation of the design oracle as a $0$-$1$ mixed-integer linear program (MILP) with solver-certified early stopping, and (ii) a fully polynomial-time lifted design that replaces the nonlinear objective with a tractable surrogate. Using the Kiefer-Wolfowitz equivalence theorem, we establish near G-optimality guarantees and characterize the induced statistical-computational trade-offs. As an application, we develop a best assortment identification algorithm for MNL bandits with linear utilities and non-uniform revenues, and prove an instance-dependent sample complexity of $\tilde{O}\big(\frac{d \log N}{\Delta^2}\big)$, where $d$ is the feature dimension, $N$ is the number of arms, and $\Delta$ is the minimum revenue gap.
items.author: Joongkyu Lee, Min-hwan Oh

items.title: Events as Triggers for Behavioral Diversity in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.12388v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Effective multi-agent cooperation requires agents to adopt diverse behaviors as task conditions evolve-and to do so at the right moment. Yet, current Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) frameworks that facilitate this diversity are still limited by the fact that they bind fixed behaviors to fixed agent identities. Consequently, they are ill-equipped for tasks where agents need to take on different roles at very specific moments in time. We argue that, to define these behavioral transitions, the missing ingredient is $\textbf{events}$. Events are changes in the state of the system that induce qualitative changes in the task. Based on this view, we introduce a framework that decouples agent identity from behavior, capturing a continuous manifold from which agents instantiate their behaviors in response to events. This framework is based on two elements. First, to build an expressive behavior manifold, we introduce Neural Manifold Diversity (NMD), a formal distance metric that remains well-defined when behaviors are transient and agent-agnostic. Second, we use an event-based hypernetwork that generates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules over a shared team policy, enabling on-the-fly agent-policy reconfiguration in response to events. We prove that this construction ensures that diversity does not interfere with reward maximization by design. Empirical results demonstrate that our framework outperforms established baselines across benchmarks while exhibiting zero-shot generalization, and being the only method that solves tasks requiring sequential behavior reassignment.
items.author: Hannes B\"uchi, Manon Flageat, Eduardo Sebasti\'an, Amanda Prorok

items.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.10931v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(\beta+1)}/{\beta}}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $\beta^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\log\beta$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $\beta$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.
items.author: Albert Alcalde, Leon Bungert, Konstantin Riedl, Tim Roith

items.title: A Cross-Layered Multi-Drone Coordination for Medical Supply Delivery during Disaster Response Management
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.09342v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Autonomous drone fleets have potential in medical supply delivery during disaster incident response. However, coordinating multiple drones in such settings introduces compounding challenges: dynamic hazards such as wind, obstacles, and intermittent connectivity, constrained energy budgets, and the need to serve patients fairly under strict deadlines and triage-based priority. We present CEDA, a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) Double Deep Q-Network algorithm augmented with a QMIX-style monotonic mixing network for cooperative multi-drone medical delivery, designed to jointly optimize triage-aware routing, multi-agent coordination, and energy-efficient navigation under dynamic uncertainty. CEDA introduces a Priority-Preserving Fair Scheduling strategy, in which a structured reward function encodes triage priority weights, outcome-level fairness and priority-ordering rewards, and complementary shaping mechanisms that discourage systematic starvation. We evaluate CEDA in a simulated grid environment with five drones serving up to fifty patients, featuring dynamic hazard zones, stochastic action failures, and dynamically spawning patients across three triage levels, and in PX4 software-in-the-loop (SITL) validation using five X500 quadrotors controlled via MAVSDK. Simulation results show that CEDA delivers over 95\% of spawned patients, reduces obstacle collisions by over 95\% across training, and achieves a weighted triage efficiency exceeding 0.90 alongside a Jain's Fairness Index of approximately 1.0 across triage classes. CEDA preserves clinical priority ordering, with Critical patients receiving the fastest response times, while achieving low and comparable mortality across all triage classes. PX4 SITL validation further shows that the learned policy retains its triage-aware behavior under continuous simulated flight and delayed-action conditions.
items.author: Aneesh Calyam, Subrahmanya Chandra Bhamidipati, Zack Murry, Sharan Srinivas

items.title: Understanding the Performance Plateau in Text-to-Video Retrieval: A Comprehensive Empirical and Linguistic Analysis
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.00826v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Text-to-video retrieval enables users to find relevant video content using natural language queries, a task that has grown increasingly important with the rapid expansion of online video. Over the past six years, research has produced numerous methods, such as dual encoders, attention-driven models, and multimodal fusion approaches; however, fundamental questions remain about model behavior, dataset influence, and query difficulty. In this work, we evaluate 14 state-of-the-art retrieval methods across 3 widely used datasets under a unified preprocessing and evaluation framework. We analyze caption characteristics, including length, clarity, semantic category, and Action vs. Scene balance, and link these to model performance. Our results show that short, clear, and simple captions, such as those describing single actions or color attributes, achieve higher recall, while complex events, multi-step activities, or fine-grained scene descriptions remain challenging for all existing models. Attention-driven architectures better handle temporally dependent or multi-step queries, whereas dual-encoder and multimodal fusion models perform well primarily on simpler or single-category captions. Cross-dataset generalization improves with larger, more diverse caption sets, but generative captions do not consistently enhance retrieval accuracy. Overall, our findings highlight key dataset factors, benchmark challenges, and the interplay between query content and model architecture, providing guidance for developing more effective text-to-video retrieval systems.
items.author: Maria-Eirini Pegia, Dimitrios Stefanopoulos, Bj\"orn {\TH}\'or J\'onsson, Anastasia Moumtzidou, Ilias Gialampoukidis, Stefanos Vrochidis, Ioannis Kompatsiaris

items.title: A Controlled Comparison of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting: Evidence from 918 Experiments
items.summary:
arXiv:2603.16886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Reliable comparison of deep learning architectures for financial forecasting requires controlled evaluation that separates architectural effects from hyperparameter tuning, random initialization, forecast horizon, and asset characteristics. We present a five-stage benchmark using equal-budget Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, category-level configuration freezing, three-seed final training, held-out metric aggregation, and rank-based statistical validation. Nine architectures from Transformer, MLP/linear, convolutional, and recurrent families are evaluated with direct multi-step prediction from five OHLCV features across 12 assets (four cryptocurrency, four foreign exchange, four equity-index instruments), using chronological 70/15/15 splits of 30,000 hourly windows per asset at 4- and 24-hour horizons. The benchmark includes 918 runs (270 optimization trials, 648 final training runs). Across 24 asset-horizon points, ModernTCN has mean rank 1.333 and the lowest RMSE in 18 points (75.0%), followed by PatchTST (mean rank 2.000). Global ranking differences are strongly supported by an Iman-Davenport test (F(8,184)=101.36, p<1e-15), with 33 of 36 Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons significant. Rankings are consistent across horizons for all 12 assets (rho>=0.683; Stouffer p=3.47e-10), while errors increase at the longer horizon. Architecture explains 99.90% of raw error variance and 68.33% after within-slot normalization excluding LSTM; seed variance contributes at most 0.04% (0.02% without LSTM). Mean directional accuracy is 50.08%. These findings provide a statistically validated comparison of nine architectures, identify ModernTCN and PatchTST as leading performers under the evaluated conditions, and offer a reproducible benchmark for multi-asset financial time-series forecasting.
items.author: Nabeel Ahmad Saidd

items.title: FlowTouch: View-Invariant Visuo-Tactile Prediction
items.summary:
arXiv:2603.08255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Tactile sensation is essential for contact-rich manipulation tasks. It provides direct feedback on object geometry, surface properties, and interaction forces, enhancing perception and enabling fine-grained control. An inherent limitation of tactile sensors is that readings are available only when an object is touched. This precludes their use during planning and the initial execution phase of a task. Predicting tactile information from visual information can bridge this gap. A common approach is to learn a direct mapping from camera images to the output of vision-based tactile sensors. However, the resulting model will depend strongly on the specific setup and on how well the camera can capture the area where an object is touched. In this work, we introduce FlowTouch, a novel model for view-invariant visuo-tactile prediction. Our key idea is to use an object's local 3D mesh to encode rich information for predicting tactile patterns while abstracting away from scene-dependent details. FlowTouch integrates scene reconstruction and Flow Matching-based models for image generation. Our results show that FlowTouch is able to bridge the sim-to-real gap and generalize to new sensor instances. We further show that the resulting tactile images can be used for downstream grasp stability prediction. Our code, datasets and videos are available at https://flowtouch.github.io/
items.author: Seongjin Bien, Carlo Kneissl, Tobias J\"ulg, Frank Fundel, Thomas Ressler-Antal, Florian Walter, Bj\"orn Ommer, Gitta Kutyniok, Wolfram Burgard

items.title: Co-optimization for Adaptive Conformal Prediction
items.summary:
arXiv:2603.01719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In regression, conformal prediction often suffers from inefficiency under heteroscedasticity and skewness due to fixed, non-adaptive interval centering. We propose CoCP, a new method that parameterizes prediction intervals by a center $m(x)$ and a radius $h(x)$, and alternates between learning $h(x)$ via smooth quantile regression on folded residuals and refining $m(x)$ using a smooth interval loss. This corrects mis-centering and drives the interval toward high-density regions. Beyond finite-sample marginal validity via split-conformal calibration, we prove that CoCP also attains asymptotic conditional coverage and optimal interval length if the base estimators are consistent. Experiments demonstrate that CoCP yields tighter intervals and achieves improved empirical conditional-coverage reliability. Code is available at https://github.com/jjoeysu/cocp.
items.author: Xiaoyi Su, Zhixin Zhou, Rui Luo

items.title: Cross-Fitted Clipped Covariance Estimation with a Data-Driven Tail-Energy Criterion
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.14020v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Heavy-tailed data make covariance estimation sensitive to the clipping level: stronger clipping reduces variance but increases bias. We study how to choose this clipping level from the data within a radial clipped covariance family. We propose the quantile tail-energy surrogate (QTES), a fully data-driven rule that combines a cross-fitted variance certificate with a held-out estimate of the tail energy removed by clipping. QTES requires no distributional prior parameters. For Euclidean clipping, the operator-norm bias is bounded by this scalar tail-energy quantity. Under a finite $L_4$ moment condition, together with a mild feasibility condition for the QTES block construction, we prove a uniform finite-sample calibration bound over a positive clipping grid and a finite-sample guarantee for the estimator selected by QTES, relative to the best candidate on that grid under the same variance-plus-bias criterion. Experiments on clean heavy-tailed and contaminated benchmarks show that QTES performs strongly across both regimes and remains competitive with the best reference methods considered.
items.author: Even He, Zaizai Yan

items.title: Expected Harm: Rethinking Safety Evaluation of (Mis)Aligned LLMs
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.01600v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Current evaluations of LLM safety predominantly rely on severity-based taxonomies to assess the harmfulness of models' responses to malicious queries. We argue that this formulation requires re-examination as it implicitly equates model output with realized harm while neglecting Execution Likelihood-the conditional probability of a threat being realized by a real-world actor given a model's response. In this work, we introduce Expected Harm, a metric that weights the severity of a jailbreak by its execution likelihood, modeled as a function of execution cost. Through empirical analysis of state-of-the-art models, we reveal a systematic Inverse Risk Calibration: models disproportionately exhibit stronger refusal behaviors for low-likelihood (high-cost) threats while remaining vulnerable to high-likelihood (low-cost) queries. Mechanistically, we first provide an analysis using linear probing, revealing that while refusal mechanisms linearly separate queries by severity, they do not use execution likelihood as an indicator for refusal. Then, we use Olmo-3's open-source staged checkpoints to trace the root cause of miscalibration to the Supervised Fine Tuning (SFT) training data distribution (82.8% of safety examples at cost levels 0-1) and show that cost representations are weak from the SFT stage onward. Finally, we demonstrate that this miscalibration creates a vulnerability: by exploiting this property, we increase the attack success rate of existing jailbreaks by up to $2\times$.
items.author: Yen-Shan Chen, Zhi Rui Tam, Cheng-Kuang Wu, Yun-Nung Chen

items.title: Parabolic Positional Encoding: A Vision-Centric, Principled, Extrapolatable, and General Approach
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.01418v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We propose Parabolic Positional Encoding (PaPE), a parabola-based positional encoding for vision modalities in attention-based architectures. Given a set of vision tokens-such as from videos, event camera streams, images, or point clouds-our objective is to encode their positions while accounting for the characteristics of vision modalities. Prior works have largely extended positional encodings from 1D-sequences in language to nD-structures in vision, but only with partial account of vision characteristics. We address this gap by designing PaPE from principles distilled from prior work: translation invariance, rotation invariance (PaPE-RI), distance decay, directionality, and context awareness. Extrapolation experiments on ImageNet-1K show how PaPE extrapolates remarkably well, improving in absolute terms by up to 10.5 over the next-best encoding. Generality experiments on 8 datasets across 4 modalities show that PaPE is a general vision positional encoding, as PaPE matches the best baseline on 5 datasets and exceeds all on 2 datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/DTU-PAS/parabolic-position-encoding.
items.author: Christoffer Koo {\O}hrstr{\o}m, Rafael I. Cabral Muchacho, Yifei Dong, Filippos Moumtzidellis, Ronja G\"uldenring, Florian T. Pokorny, Lazaros Nalpantidis

items.title: Repair Brain Damage: Real-Numbered Error Correction Code for Neural Network
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.00076v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study neural networks (NNs) operating under hardware-induced memory faults and computational errors, which can degrade reliability in safety-critical applications. To address this challenge, we propose a novel real-valued error correction coding (ECC) framework capable of detecting and correcting both types of errors. Our approach imposes structured real-valued linear constraints on network weights, enabling efficient error detection and recovery without increasing the number of parameters or compromising classification performance. The proposed method leverages linear programming and sparse recovery techniques to achieve low-complexity error correction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first real-number-based ECC scheme that simultaneously addresses memory and computational errors in neural networks.
items.author: Ziqing Lu, Myung Cho, Qiutong Jin, Weiyu Xu

items.title: DNNs, Dataset Statistics, and Correlation Functions
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.21715v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: This paper argues that dataset structure is important in image recognition tasks (among other tasks). Specifically, we focus on the nature and genesis of correlational structure in the actual datasets upon which DNNs are trained. We argue that DNNs are implementing a widespread methodology in condensed matter physics and materials science that focuses on mesoscale correlation structures that live between fundamental atomic/molecular scales and continuum scales. Specifically, we argue that DNNs that are successful in image classification must be discovering high order correlation functions. It is well-known that DNNs successfully generalize in apparent contravention of standard statistical learning theory. We consider the implications of our discussion for this puzzle.
items.author: Robert W. Batterman, James F. Woodward

items.title: Distributed Information Bottleneck Theory for Multi-Modal Task-Aware Semantic Communication
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.04000v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Semantic communication shifts the focus from bit-level accuracy to task-relevant semantic delivery, enabling efficient and intelligent communication for next-generation networks. However, existing multi-modal solutions often process all available data modalities indiscriminately, ignoring that their contributions to downstream tasks are often unequal. This not only leads to severe resource inefficiency but also degrades task inference performance due to irrelevant or redundant information. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel task-aware distributed information bottleneck (TADIB) framework, which quantifies the contribution of any set of modalities to given tasks. Based on this theoretical framework, we design a practical coding scheme that intelligently selects and compresses only the most task-relevant modalities at the transmitter. To find the optimal selection and the codecs in the network, we adopt the probabilistic relaxation of discrete selection, enabling distributed encoders to make coordinated decisions with score function estimation and common randomness. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our solution matches or surpasses the inference quality of full-modal baselines while significantly reducing communication and computational costs.
items.author: Yujie Zhou, Cheng Peng, Rulong Wang, Yong Xiao, Yingyu Li, Guangming Shi, Ping Zhang

items.title: Critically-Damped Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics for Generative Modeling
items.summary:
arXiv:2506.21741v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) represent an entirely new class of generative AI methods that have yet to be fully explored. They use Langevin dynamics, represented as stochastic differential equations, to describe a process that transforms data into noise, the forward process, and a process that transforms noise into generated data, the reverse process. Many of these methods utilize auxiliary variables that formulate the data as a ``position" variable, and the auxiliary variables are referred to as ``velocity", ``acceleration", etc. In this sense, it is possible to ``critically damp" the dynamics. Critical damping has been successfully introduced in Critically-Damped Langevin Dynamics (CLD) and Critically-Damped Third-Order Langevin Dynamics (TOLD++), but has not yet been applied to dynamics of arbitrary order. The proposed methodology generalizes Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics (HOLD), a recent state-of-the-art diffusion method, by introducing the concept of critical damping from systems analysis. Similarly to TOLD++, this work proposes an optimal set of hyperparameters in the $n$-dimensional case, where HOLD leaves these to be user defined. Additionally, this work provides closed-form solutions for the mean and covariance of the forward process that greatly simplify its implementation. Experiments are performed on the CIFAR-10 and CelebA-HQ $256 \times 256$ datasets, and validated against the FID metric.
items.author: Benjamin Sterling, Chad Gueli, M\'onica F. Bugallo

items.title: Lattice-Based Pruning of Recurrent Neural Networks via Poset Modeling: A Corrected Theory and a Matched-Sparsity Evaluation
items.summary:
arXiv:2502.16525v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Magnitude pruning of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) ignores how information flows between neurons. An earlier version proposed to model RNN dependencies as a partially ordered set (poset) and to retain the meet-irreducible elements of its dependency lattice. By Birkhoff's representation theorem, the meet-irreducible ideals of a finite poset are in bijection with its elements, so retaining them retains everything; the critical-set criterion used earlier selects precisely the elements comparable to all others, of which a dense recurrent layer has none. Condensing a thresholded dependency graph into strongly connected components yields a well-defined dependency order, a graded order score and an acyclic pruning rule; for Cohen-Grossberg networks and LSTMs, acyclic pruning makes local stability decompose over modules. For a 128-unit LSTM pruned at matched sparsity on row-wise and chunked sequential MNIST (three seeds, equal training budgets), the original rules remove every recurrent weight or equal random column pruning; the order score is no better than degree, PageRank or norm; trained weights show little directional bias; and imposing acyclicity from initialisation costs 2.1 and 10.5 percentage points at 50% and 90% sparsity. In the networks studied, order structure must be imposed rather than discovered.
items.author: Rakesh Sengupta

items.title: Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks
items.summary:
arXiv:2408.17246v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We consider the problem of learning maximal Lyapunov functions to compute the maximal region of attraction of nonlinear dynamical systems using neural networks. Two obstacles limit existing neural-network approaches: 1) finite-width approximations can fail to preserve the strict Lyapunov inequalities near the equilibrium, where they become arbitrarily weak, and 2) training is necessarily performed on a bounded computational domain for which the classical Lyapunov and Zubov theorems do not directly apply. To address these issues, first we derive Lyapunov and Zubov theorems directly on a prescribed compact computational domain, characterizing the maximal region of attraction within that domain as the solution of a boundary-value PDE. Second, we introduce the Taylor Lyapunov network, an architecture that prescribes the quadratic leading-order term via the system's linearization and represents the higher-order remainder through a structured cubic factorization, guaranteeing that any network in this class is a valid local Lyapunov function by construction. Finally, we prove that Taylor Lyapunov networks are universal approximators of maximal Lyapunov functions on compact domains, and combine these results into an unsupervised, physics-informed training procedure. Numerical experiments on systems of varying dimensions and stability types show that the proposed architecture is efficient at estimating the maximum region of attraction.
items.author: Matthieu Barreau, Nicola Bastianello

items.title: Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications
items.summary:
arXiv:2405.13302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study how the Bauer--Jost--Liu curvature bound applies to hypergraph Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) and how its accuracy depends on local mass and geometry. An explicit weighted-graph representation shows how the graph theorem applies. A transport construction transfers the bounds to monotone pairwise hyperedge aggregations. We analyze endpoint cancellation under laziness, quantify the exact improvement over the earlier mixture bound, and characterize the extremal geometry at fixed endpoint and overlap statistics. Further results quantify worst-case slack, stability, and exactness on isolated hyperedges. A capacity-constrained short-detour refinement uses additional geometric information and improves monotonically as the query budget increases. As a computational application, a threshold cascade preserves exact transport decisions. Numerical verification and public-hypergraph experiments examine tightness, walk dependence, and aggregation, including evaluations on 42,940 finite pairwise comparisons and 64,620 public-data instances. Together, the results specify the scope, equality mechanisms, and computational uses of BJL-type hypergraph bounds.
items.author: Wonwoo Kang, Heehyun Park

items.title: Discovering contemporaneous and lagged causal relations in autocorrelated nonlinear time series datasets
items.summary:
arXiv:2003.03685v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The paper introduces a novel conditional independence (CI) based method for linear and nonlinear, lagged and contemporaneous causal discovery from observational time series in the causally sufficient case. Existing CI-based methods such as the PC algorithm and also common methods from other frameworks suffer from low recall and partially inflated false positives for strong autocorrelation which is an ubiquitous challenge in time series. The novel method, PCMCI$^+$, extends PCMCI [Runge et al., 2019b] to include discovery of contemporaneous links. PCMCI$^+$ improves the reliability of CI tests by optimizing the choice of conditioning sets and even benefits from autocorrelation. The method is order-independent and consistent in the oracle case. A broad range of numerical experiments demonstrates that PCMCI$^+$ has higher adjacency detection power and especially more contemporaneous orientation recall compared to other methods while better controlling false positives. Optimized conditioning sets also lead to much shorter runtimes than the PC algorithm. PCMCI$^+$ can be of considerable use in many real world application scenarios where often time resolutions are too coarse to resolve time delays and strong autocorrelation is present.
items.author: Jakob Runge

items.title: Cumulative Marginal Matching for One-Step Diffusion
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.34575v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The sampling procedures of diffusion and flow-matching models involve hundreds of denoising steps incurring substantial inference time, which has motivated a growing body of work on training schemes for few-step and one-step generation. Existing approaches primarily seek to align the generation trajectory of few-step and base models, yet their training objectives only involve discrepancies at a single point in the trajectory, encouraging only local \emph{point-level} alignment. While recent methods such as \emph{Shortcut-CSL} introduce cumulative objective that enforce alignment over the entire trajectory, this is suboptimal as they do not directly enforce alignment between the distributions induced by the two models throughout the generation process. We propose \emph{Cumulative Marginal Matching} (CMM), a principled objective for few-step generation: by viewing flow-matching as a sequence of intermediate marginal distributions connecting the prior and data distributions, CMM directly optimizes the cumulative discrepancy between the base and few-step marginal distributions over the entire sequence. Specifically, we formulate this discrepancy using the Wasserstein-2 distance. By exploiting the pushforward representation of flow-matching, we transform an intractable cumulative Wasserstein objective into a tractable surrogate that can be optimized using samples from the intermediate marginal, which are readily generated through the conditional interpolation process of flow-matching. Furthermore, we show that the existing \emph{Shortcut-CSL} objective arises as a first-order approximation of that of the CMM, establishing a theoretical connection between the two objectives. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate improvement in generation quality over \emph{Shortcut-CSL} and other state-of-the-art one- and few-step baselines under identical training budgets.
items.author: Paribesh Regmi, Rui Li

items.title: Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.33609v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) is often proposed as a low-cost complement to multibeam surveys of ports, but its accuracy is seldom measured on an area the model has never seen. We test SDB in the turbid, shallow and tidal waters of the Abu Dhabi coast against 285,619 multibeam soundings from twelve surveys at six port areas, reduced to Lowest Astronomical Tide. The Stumpf ratio, the Lyzenga transform, a monotonic gradient-boosted tree model (LightGBM) and a U-Net ensemble were trained on 72 Sentinel-2 images and tested in transfer to an unseen site and with local control (about 20% of a site's soundings, spatial blocks beyond a 225 m buffer). The validation design changed the result more than the model: the same LightGBM model gave 0.57 m RMSE under a random pixel split, 1.30 m under spatial blocks and 1.66 m at an unseen site. In transfer the Stumpf ratio (1.45 m) was not beaten by LightGBM, the U-Net or Lyzenga. With local control a hybrid of the tree output and the band ratio reached 1.11 m over 0-11 m, 67% of pixels within the IHO S-44 Order 2 tolerance and a conformal 95% interval with 95% observed coverage; in clear water it reached 0.29-0.53 m. The seabed could not be read beyond 11 m, and summer images were five to six times more turbid than winter ones. ICESat-2 ATL24 agreed with the surveys to 0.25 m after a depth-dependent offset was removed. A 60 m reconnaissance mosaic of 17,200 km2 of the UAE coast, calibrated cell by cell on ICESat-2 without any vessel survey, reached 1.42 m RMSE on held-out blocks over half of the product. Sentinel-2 SDB with about a hundred control depths per image is a usable reconnaissance and change-monitoring tool in these waters to about 10 m; it does not meet S-44 Order 1 without local control, and accuracies from random splits should not be taken as operational accuracy.
items.author: Muhammad Saeed, Mohamed H. Alhosani, Dmitry Mikhaylov, Yasser F. Al Wahedi

items.title: Sharp Non-Asymptotic Analysis of the Penalized Challenger in $\beta$-EB-TCI for Bernoulli Bandits
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.01951v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Top-two algorithms are simple and effective for fixed-confidence best-arm identification, but their sharp non-asymptotic behavior is still not well understood. We study this question for Bernoulli bandits through $\beta$-EB-TCI, the empirical-best top-two rule of Jourdan et al., whose challenger minimizes a Bernoulli transportation cost plus a logarithmic penalty in its pull count. We first analyze the stabilized regime, in which the empirical leader has become the true best arm and its sampling fraction stays close to $\beta$. In this regime, every suboptimal arm is sampled linearly often, and, with high probability, the stopping time is at most $T_{\beta}^{\star}(\mu)\log(1/\delta)$ plus stabilization and lower-order concentration terms, with the exact fixed-$\beta$ leading coefficient. The main remaining difficulty is therefore to control when the regime is reached. For the original rule, we obtain a non-asymptotic high-probability stopping bound on every Bernoulli instance with a unique best arm. Under a finite-mean sufficient-exploration condition, the bound yields the sharp expected sample complexity; combined with the exploration result of Jourdan et al., this covers pairwise-distinct means under their tie-breaking convention. A mild forced-exploration guard, which uses only $O(\sqrt{Kt})$ pulls up to time $t$, gives a self-contained sharp expected bound for any number of arms with a unique best arm. We also identify a limitation of proof strategies that try to handle equal suboptimal means through a single index-comparison argument.
items.author: Nam Nguyen, Tuan Quang Dam

items.title: SkillEvoLean: Mutation-enhanced skill evolution for Lean provers
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.01799v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Skill evolution offers a promising way to improve large language model agents without updating their parameters, but its use in formal theorem proving remains underexplored. Existing methods mainly target natural-language reasoning, improving skills by analyzing successful and failed trajectories and incrementally revising solving strategies. Although the Lean verifier provides reliable execution feedback, when all sampled trajectories fail, existing skill evolution methods lack successful trajectories from which to infer effective update directions. Furthermore, these methods also focus mainly on the root instruction file, thus underexploring the evolution of reference knowledge including mathematical concepts and proving techniques. To address these limitations, we propose a mutation-enhanced skill self-evolution framework for building skill-augmented Lean provers. The framework jointly evolves a high-level solving policy and its reference knowledge through progressive and mutation-based updates. Progressive evolution derives local improvements from successful and failed trajectories, while mutation is triggered when no complete proof can be generated, sampling mathematical concepts to produce and select new skill candidates under verifier feedback. We evaluate our method on MiniF2F, PutnamBench, the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO 2025), and the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad (USAMO 2026). Under the same backbone model, trajectorysampling budget, and test-time compute, our method achieves proof success rates of 100.0%, 90.6%, 4/6, and 4/6, respectively, with GPT-5.5, outperforming the baseline methods. Further analysis shows that concept-guided mutation outperforms random-text-guided mutation by 6.9 and 8.2 percentage points on MiniF2F and PutnamBench, respectively, while solving one additional problem on both IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026.
items.author: Kuo Zhou, Zixiong Yang, Lu Zhang

items.title: Non-Commutative Lie-Algebraic State-Space Models: Finite-Division Variety Laws, Semidirect Cascades, and Gradient Saddle Escape
items.summary:
arXiv:2610.00329v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Structured state-space sequence models (SSMs) achieve linear-time inference and logarithmic-time parallel training via associative scans, yet diagonal transitions generate solvable semigroups unable to track non-solvable group words or 3D rigid-body manifolds. We present Non-Commutative Lie-Algebraic State-Space Models (Lie-SSMs), parameterizing recurrent updates on Lie algebra tangent spaces via the matrix exponential. First, using an o-minimal cylindrical flag collar, we establish an unconditional single-layer finite-division criterion for contracting $SO(3)$ and $SU(2)$ heads, proving odd-prime Sylow abelianity, odd-$p$-core centrality, and exponent-30 commutator obstructions excluding $S_5$ in $SO(3)^m, SU(2)^m,$ and $SO(4)^m$ while identifying the sharp threshold $d^*(S_5)=d^*(A_6)=5$ in $SO(5)$. Second, Depth-2 semidirect and Schreier $2$-cocycle cascades resolve $S_5$, $2I\cong SL_2(F_5)$, and $\mathrm{Heis}(F_p)$ in $O(\log T)$ scan depth, whereas unnormalized contracting coupling collapses exponentially without Directional RMSNorm. Third, we characterize the $\Theta(\varepsilon^{c-1})$ Chen--Magnus--Hall--Witt commutator saddle and $1/|[G,G]|$ coset-centroid dilution, proving generic first-order symmetry breaking at $\varepsilon=0$ and teacher-forced local Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz convergence under dense prefix supervision and factored readouts ($99.90\%/99.40\%$ on $S_5$ at $T=128$; $100.00\%$ on $D_{16}$). Across $SE_2(3)$ Left-Jacobian odometry, Hillis--Steele/Blelloch GPU scans ($48.24\times$ forward, $20.27\times/10.28\times$ full-layer speedup at $T=2048$), and three 3D IMU benchmarks (UCI HAR, UCI HAPT-PT, and 17-subject REALDISP), Lie-$SO(3)$ models reach $95.69\%\pm 0.14\%$ on HAR, $88.44\%\pm 0.83\%$ episode logit-vote ($83.97\%\pm 1.20\%$ C3 window in 30-subject 5-fold CV; $87.16\%\pm 0.64\%$ 9-subject split) on HAPT-PT, and $84.23\%\pm 1.00\%$ on REALDISP.
items.author: Zeyu Jia

items.title: Toward Optimal Switching Regret for Multi-Armed Bandits with Oblivious Adversary
items.summary:
arXiv:2609.13547v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study switching regret in adversarial multi-armed bandits, where the learner competes with an arm sequence that changes at most $S$ times. When $S$ is known, an optimal expected regret of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{(S+1)KT})$ is obtainable [Auer et al., 2002]. However, when $S$ is unknown, Marinov and Zimmert [2021] show that this guarantee is impossible under an adaptive adversary. In this paper, we show that a single algorithm achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{(S+1)KT})$ expected regret for every $S$ against an oblivious adversary, resolving an open problem of Auer et al. [2019b]. Our algorithm combines a fixed-share learner initialized with a small learning rate and dyadic-interval subroutines that search for local improvements using randomized learning rates and implicit exploration. Importantly, a non-uniform prior favors following the main learner, keeping the cost of maintaining many subroutines small. When the subroutines accumulate sufficient improvement over the main learner, its learning rate doubles, allowing adaptation to the unknown number of comparator switches $S$.
items.author: Mengxiao Zhang

items.title: Predicting Dose-Response Success from Primary Screening Data
items.summary:
arXiv:2608.26538v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: High-throughput drug screening uses inexpensive primary screens to select compounds for more costly follow-up dose-response experiments, which estimate compound potency (pXC50) by determining the concentration required to produce a specified biological effect. However, many promoted compounds fail to yield a reportable potency, even when activity is subsequently confirmed. We investigated whether inexpensive three-point primary-screening data could predict whether a more costly 11-point dose-response experiment would yield a reportable pXC50. Using a dataset of 32,971 compound-assay pairs with three-point primary-screening and 11-point dose-response measurements, we trained random-forest models to predict successful potency quantification. Our model achieved an AUROC of 0.939 +/- 0.002 and generalized to previously unseen chemical scaffolds and assay-mechanism families. We found that primary-screen response features were more predictive of dose-response quantifiability than molecular structure-based features. Successful potency quantification was also strongly associated with primary-screen response amplitude. Across eight chronological test releases, the model retrospectively retained 90% of reportable potencies while selecting only 55.7% of historically promoted compound-assay pairs for follow-up profiling. These findings suggest that predicting potency quantifiability from primary-screening data could improve the efficiency of compound prioritization and reduce unnecessary dose-response experiments.
items.author: Sean Lim

items.title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
items.summary:
arXiv:2608.19857v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: For AI agents to be useful beyond simple chat, they must hold sensitive user context such as calendars, credentials, health records, and financial data. We study whether the mere presence of such secrets in a model's context window introduces hidden correlations into the model's benign outputs, allowing reconstruction even when the model correctly refuses direct extraction. We further study whether an adversary can actively engineer prompts that amplify this effect, using the model as a covert carrier to transmit secrets through seemingly innocuous text. In both cases, this limited leakage is exploited using a novel adaptive attack that assumes black-box access to the underlying model. In controlled experiments across eight proprietary models, we find that 2-digit in-context secrets are reconstructed with near-perfect accuracy and 4-digit secrets at 82\% exact match, all from outputs the model produces in response to ordinary, non-adversarial requests. We observe that more capable models leak more: stronger instruction-following amplifies sensitivity to in-context secrets, suggesting leakage is a byproduct of capability as opposed to a patchable bug. We show this leakage enables two practical attacks: (1) a trained classifier that infers semantic predicates about user memories (e.g., health conditions, financial events) from routine natural-language outputs, and (2) an RL-trained adversary that extracts full Social Security Numbers from a production-style agent.
items.author: Jaiden Fairoze, Neal Mangaokar, Kamalika Chaudhuri, Sanjam Garg, Saeed Mahloujifar

items.title: Evaluating Rollout-Verified Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of a Reasoning Model for Multi-Zone Variable-Air-Volume Control
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.27914v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems account for a large share of building energy use. High-performance control often requires building-specific modeling or training, limiting scalability. We investigate whether a frontier reasoning model -- a large language model trained to use additional inference-time computation -- can coordinate multi-zone variable-air-volume control without building-specific training, and whether rollout-verified reinforcement fine-tuning can improve a smaller, locally deployable model. Five controllers were evaluated over five summer days in a physics-based four-zone emulator. Across three runs, GPT-5 used 6.8-7.4% less electricity than a Guideline 36-based baseline, but used less outdoor air and had lower CO$_2$ compliance. GPT-5 provided a capability reference for fine-tuning the smaller model. A trained reinforcement learning controller used 4.5% less electricity than the baseline while improving temperature and CO$_2$ compliance. To assess this controller's critic as a lower-cost verifier, we compared its estimates with deterministic rollout returns. Across 470 candidates, their correlation was 0.9995, yet the critic selected the best action in only 7 of 30 states. High overall correlation did not ensure reliable ranking at the same state. We fine-tuned gpt-oss-20b using rollout returns as rewards. One 200-step run produced no sustained improvement in the returns of sampled actions and no improvement in closed-loop performance. Analysis of the model's reasoning traces and quantitative tests showed that its next-state predictions of temperature and CO$_2$ were unreliable both before and after fine-tuning. Because next-state prediction is important for decision-making, these findings motivate testing whether supervised fine-tuning on next-state prediction improves subsequent rollout-verified reinforcement fine-tuning.
items.author: Takumi Shioda, Kohei Terashima, Tatsuo Nagai

items.title: MS-GPT: Rethinking MS/MS De Novo Structure Elucidation as Spectrum-Induced Posterior Querying of a Molecule-Language Model
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.23607v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) is a central inverse problem in analytical chemistry. Most existing approaches to MS/MS identification remain tied to reference libraries or predefined candidate sets, whereas de novo methods aim to generate structures directly from spectra. A common de novo route predicts a molecular fingerprint from the spectrum and then decodes structures from it, enabling decoder pretraining on large molecule-only corpora. However, this paradigm creates a training-inference mismatch: the decoder is trained on oracle fingerprints computed from molecules, but at inference it is queried with a noisy spectrum-induced fingerprint posterior that is typically collapsed to a single thresholded fingerprint. We introduce MS-GPT, which recasts fingerprint-mediated de novo elucidation as spectrum-induced posterior querying of a conditional molecule-language model. MS-GPT conditions a molecule-language model on fingerprints and formulas, then converts the spectrum-induced posterior into a band of fingerprint queries near the oracle-fingerprint manifold through active-bit density calibration. Candidates sampled across this band are pooled and ranked by generation frequency and posterior similarity. A lightweight LoRA adapter further mitigates domain-specific posterior bias while preserving the pretrained molecular prior. On NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym, MS-GPT sets a new state of the art, reaching Top-1/Top-10 exact-match accuracy of 17.1%/27.6% and 10.2%/13.2%, respectively, and candidate-pool scaling improves recovery with a near-linear increase in inference cost. The source code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/VIKI623/MS-GPT.
items.author: Xin Zhao, Yumin Liu, Zhuo Li, Weichu Zheng, Feng Zhu, Xiaokang Yang, Yaohui Jin, Yanyan Xu

items.title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.22980v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have long sought calibration-free operation, yet classifiers are typically benchmarked on discrimination alone. Discrimination is blind to calibration, a meaningful gap given that electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are nonstationary and point-estimate classifiers can become overconfident under distribution shift. We conducted a large-scale study contrasting Bayesian complete-pooling models against frequentist baselines for cross-subject, left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery EEG classification across 20 datasets. Each of six frequentist pipelines was paired with an analogous Bayesian pipeline sharing identical, deterministic feature extraction, so that only the classifier was Bayesian. Bayesian classifiers were fit via Markov chain Monte Carlo. Our primary metric was the Brier score, decomposed into reliability and resolution, alongside the area under the ROC curve for discrimination and Shannon entropy for sharpness. For each metric we fit a random-effects meta-analysis with Knapp-Hartung adjustment, verified by leave-one-out influence analysis. Bayesian complete-pooling produced statistically significant improvements in reliability and increases in predictive uncertainty (lower sharpness), with 95% confidence intervals of [-0.0029, -0.0001] for reliability and [0.0022, 0.0220] bits for entropy. Still, neither effect held statistical significance when datasets with flagged posterior sampling were excluded. Brier score, resolution, and discrimination showed no significant differences. Between-study heterogeneity was low across all metrics. Bayesian pipelines consumed roughly thirteen times more energy than their frequentist counterparts, a cost that remains modest relative to common household appliances. This modest cost makes partial-pooling across subjects and sessions, the structure complete-pooling omits, a feasible next step.
items.author: Ethan Davis

items.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.21535v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by having a draft propose tokens that a target verifies in parallel. Frontier models increasingly ship a built-in Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft head, assumed to be cheap beside verification. A shipped full-attention MTP head can become disproportionately expensive beside a hybrid target at long context. The head attends over the full KV cache for each of $\gamma$ draft forwards per decode step, while only 9-25% of target layers retain full attention, so a single draft layer can issue context reads at a rate comparable to the whole target. On hard, low-acceptance workloads, deep native MTP becomes net-negative: slower than no speculation.
  We apply a StreamingLLM-style window plus attention sink to the draft only (Windowed-MTP); target verification remains full-context, so the target distribution is preserved. The intervention is training-free and drop-in. On three models from two hybrid families (Gated DeltaNet and Mamba2) at 1M context on one GPU in SGLang, it provides an acceptance-free 1.28-1.44x per-decode-step speedup over native MTP. The speedup grows with context; at matched acceptance, TPOT improves by the same factor. The window removes most of the draft's working set, and a compact ring buffer converts that reduction into physical capacity: it reclaims the otherwise dead draft pool, a measured 7.7-11.1% of total KV at 1M, making room for one additional concurrent 1M request in the Qwen-35B batch sweep.
items.author: Alagappan Valliappan

items.title: On the Design Space of Discrete Diffusion Online Adaptation for Molecular Optimization
items.summary:
arXiv:2607.02834v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Molecular optimization often starts from a pretrained generative model that captures a broad prior over valid molecular structures. At test time, however, the goal is not to sample from this prior, but to use a limited oracle budget to shift generation toward task-specific high-reward molecules. We study this adaptation problem for discrete diffusion models. Each online round couples several choices. The loop must decide which candidates to evaluate, how rewards become model updates, which feedback to reuse, and how far to move beyond the pretrained prior. These choices have mostly been studied in isolation, leaving open whether they complement one another, become redundant, or interfere inside a full online adaptation loop. We conduct controlled studies across six small-molecule binding-affinity tasks and three protein-fitness tasks. We find that acquisition, reward shaping, and model debiasing provide complementary routes to higher reward, especially for small molecules. Replay further stabilizes learning, while validity penalties keep small-molecule exploration on the valid molecular manifold. Together, these findings point to a practical recipe for feedback-efficient molecular optimization: online fine-tuning with acquisition, reward shaping, debiasing, replay, and validity control. This recipe outperforms offline fine-tuning and inference-time search baselines under matched oracle-call budgets and GPU-hour accounting. The gains are largest when high-reward candidates require larger shifts from the pretrained prior.
items.author: Trevor Chen, Ariel Dai, Jason Yang, Riccardo De Santi, Daniel Khalil, Wenda Chu, Nate Gruver, Pranav Murugan, Alexander F. G. Goldberg, Maruan Al-Shedivat, Yisong Yue

items.title: MIRAGE: Auditing Anti-Muslim Bias in Frontier LLMs Across Reasoning, Agentic, and Time-Coupled Conditions
items.summary:
arXiv:2606.16562v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Five years after the discovery of persistent anti-Muslim bias in large language models, most evaluations remain confined to single-turn prompt completion, a setting that no longer reflects how frontier LLMs are deployed. We introduce \textbf{MIRAGE} (Muslim-Identity Reasoning and Agentic Generation Evaluation), a benchmark of 1{,}200 prompts spanning three deployment-realistic conditions: direct completion, chain-of-thought reasoning, and simulated agentic decision-making across content moderation, lending triage, refugee claim summarization, and hiring screens. Across six frontier models, we find that (i) chain-of-thought reasoning \emph{amplifies} rather than suppresses Muslim-violence associations by 12--34\% relative to direct completion, (ii) agentic decisions exhibit a 9--22 percentage-point asymmetry between Muslim and matched non-Muslim cases on identical evidence, and (iii) bias is sharply time-coupled to retrieved news context, increasing 18--27\% under recent-conflict retrieval. Existing prompt-based mitigations transfer poorly across our three conditions, suppressing direct-completion bias while leaving agentic asymmetry largely intact. We release MIRAGE and an open evaluation harness to support targeted mitigation research.
items.author: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Tamim Sheikh

items.title: AME: A Multi-Type Contributor Attribution Framework in Generative AI Markets
items.summary:
arXiv:2606.16075v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Generative AI enables value creation through multi-stage collaboration among heterogeneous contributors, including training data, base models, fine-tuning behaviors, and prompts. However, how to fairly allocate the data value remains largely unexplored. This paper formulates multi-stage generative AI value allocation as a new research problem and identifies three core challenges: heterogeneous data contribution valuation, data rights mapping, and trustworthy execution. We propose AME (Attribution-Mapping-Execution) framework, a unified framework that integrates data contribution valuation, data rights mapping, and trustworthy execution into a single workflow. Experimental results demonstrate that AME framework achieves data value allocation outcomes more consistent with human reference judgments while maintaining low-cost trustworthy execution. Our work provides an initial foundation for value assessment and revenue allocation in generative AI data markets.
items.author: Yang Shi, Songwen Pei, Yang Gao, Bingxue Zhang

items.title: How to Score Experts for One-Shot MoE Expert Pruning: A Systematic Formulation and Selection Principle
items.summary:
arXiv:2606.15716v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models reduce per-token computation through sparse expert activation, yet deployment still requires storing the full expert pool, making one-shot expert pruning a practical approach for reducing memory usage. Although effective, existing criteria are largely heuristic, and no single criterion is universally optimal. Thus, establishing a principle for selecting pruning criteria suited to different deployment objectives remains an important yet largely underexplored problem in one-shot expert pruning. To this end, we introduce a systematic formulation for one-shot MoE expert pruning organized around three factors: routing frequency, gate weighting, and activation strength. The formulation yields a criteria selection principle: task-agnostic pruning should favor routed-token-averaged, gate-free activation-based criteria, whereas task-specific pruning can benefit from retaining routing-frequency and gate-weight information. Beyond this principle, the formulation also provides a systematic view of existing heuristic criteria and gives rise to two new task-agnostic criteria, Mean Activation Norm (MAN) and Mean Squared Activation Norm (MSAN). Across four representative MoE models and 16 diverse benchmarks, MAN and MSAN are consistently strong in the task-agnostic setting, obtain the top-two average ranks, and improve average performance by 4.0 points on average and up to 8.8 points over the strongest baseline.
items.author: Zongfang Liu, Jinghui Zhang, Zijian Ma, Guangyi Chen, Xin Yuan

items.title: Query Entity-Oriented Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Graph Completion
items.summary:
arXiv:2606.05639v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims at predicting missing triplets from incomplete knowledge graphs, which is crucial for downstream applications. Recently, Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based methods have achieved remarkable success by performing message passing over a local subgraph centered on the query entity. In these methods, the query relation conditions message computation and aggregation, whereas the query entity serves only as a structural anchor for subgraph extraction. The query relation thus constitutes the sole explicit signal for evidence selection, even though the relevant evidence for the same relation can differ substantially across query entities. We propose Q-GNN, which incorporates the query entity as an explicit conditioning signal. Q-GNN characterizes the query entity by its local structural context and semantic type, and thus remains applicable in the inductive setting. The structural context, encoded by a dedicated encoder, modulates each message through feature-wise linear modulation, while the semantic type guides neighborhood attention and candidate scoring. Experiments in both transductive and inductive settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
items.author: Dongxiao He, Ruqiong Zhang, Zhizhi Yu, Ling Ding, Di Jin, Guangquan Xu, Zhiyong Feng

items.title: Conveyance: A Versatile Framework for Learning in Structured Class Spaces
items.summary:
arXiv:2605.28420v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: While machine learning (ML) architectures have evolved rapidly to account for complex data, loss functions like cross-entropy remain mostly structure-agnostic in many real-world applications. However, the "class-symmetric" nature of these standard losses fundamentally limits the ability of ML models to exploit structural relationships between classes, particularly when facing structured noise.
